summary: Complete Q1 Proposal review of 116 finished with changes-requested. The bundle is well scoped and carries the approved Explore's Core-owned provenance and review-binding design, but it fails strict OpenSpec validation because the added Bootstrap legacy requirement is not parsed as containing a MUST/SHALL. More importantly, review-apply is allowed to publish a verificationSummaryRef to the active Change path, then archive relocates verification.md; Reader's required replacement validation will make that already-terminal review Run conflict after a normal archive. The Proposal needs a durable archive-resolution rule for existing verification references, not merely archive non-eligibility for newly written ones.

blockingFindings.title: Proposal delta fails strict OpenSpec requirement syntax
blockingFindings.evidence: npx openspec validate execution-model-correction --strict fails: ADDED requirement Bootstrap legacy metadata correction 必须是有界例外 must contain SHALL or MUST. 116 nevertheless records openspecStrict=passed. Canonical-spec-only validation passes but does not validate this unmerged Change delta.
blockingFindings.impact: The Proposal cannot enter an approved state while its own required delta is structurally invalid, and the recorded validation fact is inaccurate.
blockingFindings.requiredResolution: Correct the added Requirement so the strict parser recognizes an explicit MUST/SHALL in its requirement body, then rerun and record openspec validate execution-model-correction --strict. Keep the change limited to the delta structural correction and accurate Run evidence.

blockingFindings.title: Archive breaks an already-published review-apply verification ResultRef
blockingFindings.evidence: The design makes only review-apply create verificationSummaryRef at openspec/changes/<context.changeId>/verification.md and makes archive non-eligible. But a review-apply Run is terminal before archive. Archive subsequently relocates Change artifacts to openspec/changes/archive/<date>-<change-id>/. Reader is required to validate persisted ResultRefs and treat missing targets as FactConflict, yet the Proposal defines no archive-aware resolver, stable logical locator, or retained source path for the existing review-apply ref. Excluding the archive Run from creating a new ref does not preserve the earlier one.
blockingFindings.impact: After an ordinary successful archive, reopening formal facts can fail closed on the formerly valid review-apply Run. That makes archive incompatible with the Proposal's own durable ResultRef and Reader contracts.
blockingFindings.requiredResolution: Define one archive-safe lifecycle for verificationSummaryRef already published by review-apply: either preserve its immutable canonical target for the reference lifetime, or make the shared resolver explicitly locate the archived verification artifact using immutable Change/archive facts while retaining an unambiguous stable reference identity. Apply the rule consistently to publication, preflight, Reader validation, archive behavior, and tests. Cover review-apply publication, archive relocation, and post-archive Reader validation of the same terminal Run.

nonBlockingFindings.title: Explore source links remain checkout-specific
nonBlockingFindings.evidence: The cited code links use file:///D:/Projects/flowkit absolute paths and cannot resolve in another checkout or platform.
nonBlockingFindings.recommendedResolution: Convert source links to repository-relative Markdown links in a future in-scope edit. This does not block the Proposal findings above.
